2. The respondent No. 1, herein, filed the above mentioned writ petition seeking a direction to the respondents to implement the judgment and order dated 11-4-2002 passed by the Member, Bhumi Appeal Board and the judgment and order dated 24-11-2002 passed by the Member, Bhumi Appeal Board in Case No. 2-20/2001-VP Appeal (Chapai Nawabgonj) and Case No. 2-168/2002 Review (Chapai Nawabgonj) respectively allowing the appeal and rejecting the review application and reversing the judgment and order dated 4-9-1999 passed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi Division in connection with VP Case No. 1140 of 1977 and VP Lease Case No.1 of 1086, releasing 0.84 acre of land out of 3.44 acres of land appertaining to SA Khatian No. 321, Plot No. 509 of mouza Jotpratap, Police Station-Sadar from the list of vested property. 

 3. The writ petitioner's case as stated in the writ petition, in short was that 3.44 acres of land of CS Plot No. 509 of mouza Jotpratap. Police Station-Sadar, District-Chapai Nawabgonj along with other lands originally belonged to Jitendra Nath Saha. That Jitendra Nath Saha sold 2.60 acres of land out of these 3.44 acres of land of CS Plot No. 509 in favour of Nawabgonj College by registered kabala dated 26-2-1957. Jitendra Nath Saha sold another 0.20 acre of land to one Saiful Islam by registered kabala. Jitendra Nath Saha had 0.64 acre of land in the suit, plot and he had been possessing the same. That during SA operation the SA khatian No. 321 was prepared in the name of Nawabgonj College and Jitendra Nath Saha, but during RS operation, the RS khatian No.6 in respect of 2.60 acres of land was prepared in the name of Nawabgonj College and RS khatian No. 243 was prepared in the name of Jitendra Nath Saha in respect of 0.6368 acre of land and the rest of the land of CS Plot No. 509 was recorded in the name of other transferee Saiful Islam. That Jitendra Nath Saha was living in the then East Pakistan and thereafter in Bangladesh all the time and possessed his 0.6368 acre of land of the suit plot along with other lands. That since some vested quarter, took attempt to grab the said 0.6368 acre of land of plot No. 509 along with other lands of Jitendra Nath Saha, he filed Other Class Suit No. 404 of 1977 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi praying for a declaration that he was a citizen of Bangladesh and also for declaration of his title in the suit land. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Rajshahi and the custodian of vested non-resident property of Rajshahi contested that suit by filing written statement. The learned Subordinate Judge, on consideration of evidence adduced by both the parties, decreed the suit on contest by the judgment and decree dated 29-5-1981 holding that Jitendra Nath Saha was a citizen of Bangladesh and declaring his title in all the scheduled properties excepting the land of plot No. 509 on the ground that the suit land of plot No. 509 was in possession of Nawabgonj College and also declared that the suit land was not enemy or vested property. That during pendency of that title suit, Jitendra Nath Saha, by a registered power of attorney dated 27-2-1981, appointed one Bhadra Kumar Mondal as his attorney to look after, manage and to transfer his landed properties. The said attorney Bhadra Kumar Mondal sold 0.20 acre of land of CS plot No. 509 in favour of the petitioner by registered kabala dated 31-10-1981. The said attorney transferred 0.44 acre of land of the same plot in favour of one Rawshan Akhtar by registered kabala dated 10- 11-1981. Subsequently said Rawshan Akhtar sold that 0.44 acre of land of the petitioner and thus the petitioner acquired title and possession in 0.64 acre of land of suit plot No. 509. The petitioner got his name mutated in respect of his purchased 0.64 acre of land and paid rent up to 1391 BS and obtained dakhilas. That since the vested property authority started BP Case No. 1140 of 1977 to declare the land of Jitendra Nath Saha as vested property Jitendra Nath Saha himself instituted the aforementioned other Class Suit No. 404 of 1977. However, after passing of the judgment and decree as aforesaid in the said Other Class Suit No. 404 of 1977, the shares of Manindra and Fanindra in plot No. 3 only has been treated as vested property. That the land of Jitendra Nath Saha was not treated as vested or enemy property. That the petitioner while he was owning and possessing his purchased 0.64 acre of land of plot No. 509, the local vested property authority started VP Case No.1 of 1986 for leasing out the case land in favour of Nawabgonj College, claiming the case land to be vested property. Knowing about that VP Case No. 1 of 1986 the petitioner filed an application before the local Vested Property authority on 22-8-1992 praying for release of the case land from the vested property list. But the Deputy Commissioner, Nawabgonj rejected the said application of the petitioner though the learned government pleader and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) recommended for release of the case land in favour of the petitioner. Against that order of the Deputy Commissioner, Nawabgonj to petitioner preferred appeal before the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi and the learned Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi sent the case record to the Deputy Commissioner, Nawabgonj with recommendation for release of the case land. But the Deputy Commissioner, Nawabgonj by his order dated 18-12-1997 expressed his inability to release the case land from the Vested Property list. Thereafter the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Nawabgonj sent the case record to the Ministry of land for opinion as to whether the case land can be released from the vested property or not. The Ministry of Land sent the case record to the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi and the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi by his order dated 15-2-1999 notified the parties, fixing 22-7-1999 for hearing. Ultimately the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi after hearing both the par- ties disallowed the appeal by order dated 4-7-1999. Against that judgment and order passed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner. Rajshahi the petitioner preferred appeal before the hairman, Bhumi Appeal Board being Case No. 2-20/2001 VP Appeal (Chapai Nawabgonj). The learned Member of Bhumi Appeal Board after hearing the arguments of the parties and on consideration of materials on record, allowed that appeal by the judgment and order dated 11-4-2002 holding that the property was not enemy /vested property and, as such, the proper- ty may be released from the category of Vested Property, Against that judgment and order of the Member of Bhumi Appeal Board, the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Chapai Nawabgonj filed Review Case No.2-168/2002 review (Chapai Nawabgonj) which was ultimately rejected after hearing by the judgment and order dated 24-11- 2002. After rejection of that review case the Deputy Commissioner, Chapai Nawabgonj filed an application before the full board of Bhumi Appeal Board on 5-5-2005 and the learned Chairrnan,Bhumi Appeal Board by order dated 13-6-2005 admitted that application and stayed the operation of the judgments and orders impugned.
